data.problem: Standard attention materializes N×N score/probability matrices in HBM, making memory and I/O quadratic in sequence length. FlashAttention eliminates these intermediates with tiling and online softmax, but its first implementation still reaches only roughly 25〜50% of A100 theoretical throughput because expensive non-matmul FP32 operations remain, long-sequence/small-batch cases expose too few thread blocks, and split-K warp partitioning forces intermediate writes, synchronization, and reads through shared memory.
data.novelty: FlashAttention-2 preserves exact tiled attention while attacking GPU execution inefficiencies left after I/O reduction. It delays output rescaling and stores only logsumexp to reduce non-matmul FLOPs, parallelizes along sequence blocks in addition to batch/head dimensions to raise SM occupancy, and changes intra-block warp partitioning from splitting K/V to splitting Q so each warp owns its output slice and avoids cross-warp reductions. It also supports causal masking, MQA and GQA without explicit KV duplication.
data.method_overview: Inputs Q,K,V reside in HBM. The forward kernel partitions Q into row blocks and K/V into column blocks. Each thread block owns a Q row block, loads it to SRAM, then streams K/V blocks from HBM. For every tile it computes QK^T with Tensor-Core-friendly matmul, updates running row maximum and exponential sum for online softmax, and accumulates an unscaled output tile times V. Instead of repeatedly normalizing the output, it keeps the output unscaled until all K/V tiles are consumed, then performs one final normalization and writes output O plus row-wise logsumexp L to HBM. This computes exactly softmax(QK^T)V without materializing N×N S or P. Across the GPU, independent Q row blocks are scheduled as separate thread blocks, adding sequence-length parallelism when batch×heads is too small to fill SMs. Within each block, warps split Q rows while sharing K/V, so each warp accumulates a distinct output slice without shared-memory reduction. Backward reloads Q/K/V/O/dO and L, recomputes attention probabilities on chip, accumulates dQ/dK/dV, and parallelizes column blocks with atomic additions for shared dQ. The result is the same attention output/gradients with O(N) auxiliary memory but higher occupancy, fewer non-matmul operations, and less shared-memory traffic.

components.name: 非行列積演算の削減
components.description: A100ではFP16/BF16 Tensor Core matmulの理論性能が312 TFLOPs/sなのに対し非matmul FP32は19.5 TFLOPs/s程度なので、少数のscalar/vector操作でも高価になる。FlashAttention-2は各tileでoutputを正規化せずunscaled accumulatorを維持し、loop終了時だけ最終scaleを適用する。またbackward用にrow maxとexp sumを別々に保存せずlogsumexp Lだけを保存する。入出力は変えず、Tensor Coreが処理できない演算割合を減らしてkernel時間をmatmulへ寄せる。

components.name: 系列長方向thread-block並列化
components.description: 初代FlashAttentionは主にbatch×headごとに1 thread blockを割り当てるため、長系列でbatchが小さい場合はA100の108 SMを埋められない。FlashAttention-2はforwardのQ row blocksを独立したthread blocksとして並列実行し、batch/headに加えてsequence dimensionからも並列度を得る。backwardではK/V column blockごとにthread blockを割り当て、共有されるdQ更新だけatomic addで統合する。長文脈ほどblock数が増えるため低occupancyを改善する。

components.name: warp間work partitioning再設計
components.description: 初代forwardのsplit-Kでは4 warpsがK/Vを分割して同じQへ掛けるため、各warpの部分outputをshared memoryへ書き、同期し、合算する必要がある。FlashAttention-2はQをwarps間で分割し、K/Vを共有する。各warpは自分のQ sliceからattention scoreとoutput sliceを最後まで担当でき、warp間reductionが不要になる。backwardもsplit-Kを避ける方向へ分割し、より複雑な依存で残る同期はあるもののshared-memory read/writeを減らす。

components.name: exact tiled attentionとmask/MQA/GQA
components.description: HBMからQ/K/Vの小tileだけをSRAMへ載せ、online softmaxでrunning max・sumを更新しながらOを累積するためN×N score/probabilityをHBMへ書かない。causal maskでは未来側だけのblockを丸ごとskipし、境界blockだけmaskする。MQA/GQAでは複数query headsが共有するK/V headを物理複製せずindexingで参照し、backward時だけ共有headへのgradientを合算する。これらはattention値を近似せず、standard attentionと同じ結果を返す。

data.system_design: FlashAttention-2はアルゴリズム複雑度O(N²d)自体を変えず、データ移動とGPU上の仕事配置を最適化する。初代FlashAttentionのHBM↔SRAM tilingを土台に、非Tensor-Core処理を削り、thread-block数をsequence方向へ増やし、warp間通信を減らす三層の最適化を重ねる。block sizeは通常64/128の組合せをhead dimensionとshared-memory/register制約に応じて手動選択し、大きすぎるblockによるregister spillを避ける。
